releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Maintenance release; see the original release page for its change list.

releases.title: Miner onboarding
changes: everycli miner register-hotkey: verify finalized subnet membership and save the public identity. No chain transaction or registration fee.
everycli miner set-api-keys: hidden prompts for Phala and nine generation providers; no dotenv file required.
remove-api-key and apply-api-keys: local credential management and explicit, guarded application to an attested worker.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Run everycli miner init after registering your hotkey and saving your API keys. The CLI proves ownership and fetches the signed deployment automatically.
No invitation file, miner token or registry login is needed for new public deployments. --invitation remains an optional legacy import.
Deployment binds the exact app automatically; hardware attestation is still required before provider activation.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: everycli miner balances displays remaining account credits in USD, with source, age and stale indicators. Supports Fal, Phala credited funds and OpenRouter account credits; unavailable/unsupported checks never appear as a fabricated zero.
everycli miner offers now displays a readable model/status/discount-percentage table. --json remains machine-readable. Discounts apply to the base miner reward, not provider charges.

everycli miner balances --publish explicitly syncs amounts/statuses/timestamps to your miner's private coordinator view for hotkey-only access on a second device. Snapshots are owner-reported and stale after 15 minutes; there is no automatic background sync.

releases.title: Top-level miner commands
changes: Moves miner setup, health, balances, offers and lifecycle commands to the top level while retaining namespaced compatibility aliases.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Short API keys now explain: “That key looks too short (minimum 10 characters).” Invalid input does not replace an existing key.
A missing wallet is named explicitly, with available local wallet names. Discovery reads directory names, never private key contents.
Registration prints its fee/transaction notice once and shows placeholder instructions only when placeholders remain.

everycli doctor explains when a key is saved locally but excluded by the signed deployment. This is not an API authentication verdict.
The worker accepts Vivix results from its reviewed clipgen-us.vivi-x.ai CDN, without forwarding credentials or allowing arbitrary hosts/redirects.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: everycli health: read-only, color-coded readiness tables with PASS, WARN and FAIL states. Checks include the local profile, release permissions, coordinator, cloud workload, fresh heartbeat and attestation session, routing, and worker support for active model offers.
everycli status now shows human-readable deployment, routing, offers and job-activity tables by default. everycli status --json retains the existing structured fields.
everycli health --json provides structured checks. Health exits with code 0 only when every readiness check passes; otherwise code 2.

Reports and displays native W credits. A credits are separate and never substituted; no USD conversion is invented.
Missing or duplicate W entries, endpoint errors and unexpected responses are unavailable, not zero. The endpoint is undocumented and may change.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Guided setup, API-key management, offers, health, balances and worker controls.
Loopback-only server, single-use pairing, private key storage and explicit paid-action confirmations.
Setup inputs survive background refresh. Pending starts/shutdowns have re-sync controls.

actions.when: If applying the Fal, transfer or Vivix worker fixes.
If your existing profile still has expiring legacy authorization.
After reconnecting a legacy authorization, apply it once and wait for fresh attestation.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Test API keys with free, read-only provider requests before saving in the UI. Rejected replacements leave existing keys untouched; restricted or unreachable checks are explicitly marked unverified, never falsely reported as accepted.
Keep setup on the selected step after saving keys. Preserve drafts during background refresh, shorten long worker names, and allow local renaming.
Remove expiry clutter from the dashboard without weakening authorization checks.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Dashboard identity: miner UID from the last finalized registration check, shortened hotkey, full-address tooltip/copy and a read-only Refresh UID action. UID 0 is valid; missing or mismatched lookups are never presented as known UIDs.

everycli reconnect and Worker → Reconnect profile recover superseded local miner authorization with proof from the same hotkey and confirmation. Exact signed identity/workload checks preserve API keys, labels and deployment history. A durable owner-only journal permits interrupted local commits to finish without repeating remote requests. Uncertain cloud operations remain blocked; no VM is created, deleted, updated or started by reconnect.
Coordinator HTTP 401 now identifies rejected miner authorization separately from Phala credential errors, with clock-check and reconnect guidance.

actions.when: If your saved authorization has been superseded; use the same hotkey.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Select your hotkey becomes Your hotkey once attached. Reopened setup shows the saved identity and its last verified UID; Check registration remains a read-only chain check.

Deploy automatically refreshes coordinator-rejected authorization once using the matching attached hotkey, before any paid cloud request. Legacy profiles without a saved signer path can find the same hotkey in the standard wallet directory. Missing, unreadable, or mismatched files still require attention.
Attaching the same hotkey again with init safely refreshes an existing public profile without discarding API keys or deployment history.

actions.when: If an attached public hotkey profile needs authorization recovery.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: A fresh profile cannot create a paid second VM while another app is still bound.
An unbound deployment can refresh a newer reviewed server release before any paid submission. Signed identity and exact OS hash validation remain mandatory.
Production dstack versions are no longer hardcoded to 0.5.9. Development and GPU image names remain disallowed; the server must review and approve the OS.

actions.when: If recovering a public profile with no local VM record.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Hide unintegrated catalog entries in CLI/UI. Integrated models that need a provider key, current pricing or a worker update retain actionable labels.

Overview shows all-time jobs by model. Use everycli jobs in the terminal, or everycli jobs --json for structured output. Completed counts mean distinct accepted jobs; failed/cancelled columns count attempts, not wallet payments.
Overview and everycli earnings show readable serving-fee tables, not nested JSON. Serving fees are accounting, not proof of alpha or cash received.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Recover an interrupted initial VM preparation with everycli reconcile, also available as Re-sync operation in the browser UI.
Requires a verified, unbound, idle coordinator and a complete successful Phala inventory without the signed VM name or prepared app ID.
Archives the abandoned preparation before clearing it. Keeps credentials, registration, label and signed configuration. Performs no cloud mutation.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Reports fixed moderation, invalid-request, billing, timeout, provider and output failure categories instead of treating every terminal error as generic.
Preserves existing Vivix moderation/parameter errors and Fal exhausted-balance errors through the worker's signed failure report.
Retries retain the same attempt and failure category. Timeouts and generic HTTP errors never trigger a reasonless legacy fallback or another paid generation.

actions.when: If applying provider-failure reporting to an existing worker.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: Distinguish Everyframe contract IDs from actual provider API IDs in the CLI and model dashboard. Do not paste studio/ or direct/ IDs into provider APIs.
Separate candidates and retired models from supported models. Block new offers for removed/deprecated endpoints while preserving withdrawal and job history.

Check OpenRouter's key-filtered model list, Vivix's workspace list, and Fal's public catalog before advertising worker capabilities. Other account access is explicitly unchecked; catalog presence is not a paid-generation guarantee.

actions.when: If applying the provider-availability worker fixes.

releases.title: CLI improvements
changes: CLI release signing is postponed. Updates and fresh installs keep SHA-256 checksums, restricted HTTPS downloads and atomic replacement. They do not fetch .sig files or require OpenSSL or a signing secret. Checksums are not independent publisher authentication. TEE, worker configuration and job-receipt signatures are unchanged and remain enforced.
Publishing uses the GitHub release environment (configure required reviewers), and an older-line hotfix no longer becomes the "latest" release.
A cargo install build is never replaced by auto-update; everycli update tells you to run cargo install again instead.

actions.when: If applying the updated worker behavior on the existing VM.

Reference video/audio and unordered image sets are rejected before billing.

releases.title: Miner authorization and API balances
changes: Miner authorizations do not expire. An outdated setup configuration refreshes automatically before management changes, using the existing authorization and preserving the worker.
Reconnecting a legacy enrollment now enables non-expiring authorization without changing its VM or offers.
The API Keys page shows provider balances, status and the last check time. Refreshing balances preserves key drafts, and saved keys can be checked before miner initialization.

actions.when: Only if status reports legacy expiring authorization; use the same hotkey.
After reconnecting legacy authorization, apply it once and wait for fresh attestation.

releases.title: Fal availability and worker recovery
changes: Restores Fal model availability after provider retirements. Confirmed models stay available when another catalog request fails or is rate-limited, and checks stop sending requests after a rate limit.
Recognizes LTX 2 Pro as retired. Workers also receive a signed list of retired models, allowing future retirements to be handled without another worker release. This list can only disable models.
Fixes stale-attestation errors for healthy workers with a valid admitted session and a fresh heartbeat. Expired sessions, workload binding and fresh attestation after a restart remain enforced.

actions.when: If your worker uses Fal and needs the availability fix.
Only if status reports legacy expiring authorization; use the same hotkey.
After reconnecting legacy authorization, apply it once and wait for fresh attestation.

releases.title: Pika H3 Flex

Supports 5–15-second text, first/last-frame and image/video/audio reference generation with native audio. 480p/768p are native; 1080p, 2K and 4K use Pika's upscaler.
Uses Pika's exact aspect-ratio buckets and frame-grid duration when validating output and quoting miner work.

actions.when: If serving Pika H3 Flex or applying the large-video delivery improvements.

releases.title: More reliable miner setup and controls
changes: Batch discounts update eligible models together and name any skipped models. An unavailable existing offer can still be withdrawn, and a temporary worker check no longer prevents an authorized, priced bid.
Guided setup includes Pika and direct Kling alongside the other providers.
Worker labels follow the observed cloud state, and unavailable lifecycle actions stay disabled.

releases.title: Worker updates and setup progress
changes: A dedicated Worker software panel shows the installed release and update status, with controls to check, install, continue or cancel a worker update.
Setup reaches 8/8 once accepting work is confirmed. Warnings about individual models remain visible separately.
Continue a saved update directly from the UI or CLI while preserving its reconciled signed release.

actions.when: If an earlier update stopped with unapproved_running_compose.
After reconciliation, continue the recorded update on the same profile.

releases.title: Worker updates wait for status recovery
changes: Temporary gateway errors, including HTTP 502, during status checks no longer end an otherwise progressing worker update. The command waits and continues from its saved stage.
Temporary heartbeat, session and attestation delays are checked again before restoring work.
Completion requires confirmation of the intended accepting/paused state. If the wait limit is reached, progress stays saved for later continuation.

actions.when: If an update is already pending, continue it using the same profile.

releases.title: Easier model and provider offers
changes: New model offers default to 0% discount. Zero-percent and inactive offers use a neutral color.
The Not offered tab shows models without an active offer. Model labels, provider counts and the overview link open that filtered view directly.
Provider switches turn offers on or off together. Turning on keeps saved discounts and uses 0% for new models; turning off withdraws offers and keeps their discounts for later.

actions.when: If adopting the added models, review and explicitly enable the offers you want to serve.

releases.title: Deleted worker recovery
changes: everycli reconnect checks that the old VM is gone, asks before retiring its old authorization, and fetches the current reviewed deployment.
Deploy worker then creates a fresh VM using that approved OS image.
Saved API keys, model offers, discounts and deletion history are preserved.

actions.when: If a deleted VM remains bound or its approved OS image has retired; retain the original profile.

releases.title: Redesigned dashboard and cumulative upgrade guidance
changes: Redesigned miner dashboard, live startup checks, a health ring, clearer progress and a new EveryFrame Miner icon.
Show every release between the installed and target CLI versions, with conditional worker-update and other follow-up steps.
Retain successful update history for dashboard notifications and automatic-update status.
Restore new Phala deployments with the current gateway parameter and show redacted validation reasons and request IDs. Existing signed configuration checks remain enforced.
Add Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash through Google directly, Fal and OpenRouter, with native Google routing first when the request is compatible.
Add the separate MiniMax H3 offer through OpenRouter. Existing worker images and model offers remain unchanged until explicitly updated.
Report provider-defined failure codes and messages, including unfamiliar reasons, for API and website explanations with credential redaction.
Add GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Flare through direct OpenAI, Fal and OpenRouter, with compatible native routes first and separate model offers.

Add opt-in automatic offers with provider-price previews, miner-selected models, discount ceilings, cost buffers and estimated exposure limits. Off by default; the worker refreshes prices while the dashboard is closed.

actions.when: If serving Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, GPT Image 2.6 or OpenRouter H3, or enabling provider error-message reporting or automatic offers, install the compatible signed worker after its release.

If adopting the new models, review their pricing and explicitly enable the offers you want to serve. Automatic offers require explicitly selecting models and reviewing limits; an upgrade never enables them.

releases.title: WaveSpeedAI and video automatic offers
changes: Add WaveSpeedAI key management, USD balance checks and 85 image, video and audio endpoints, including WaveSpeed-hosted Z-Image, Qwen Image 3, Seedream and H3 models.

Remove Fal public-catalog polling from workers and the coordinator. Use cached authenticated worker key checks; transient check failures no longer disable every Fal model. Reviewed retirements and confirmed invalid keys remain blocked.
Extend opt-in Fal automatic offers to 10 video contracts. Compare endpoint-specific prices for text, image and reference inputs and preserve configured cost limits.
Improve automatic-offer forms with explicit missing-limit guidance and preview details.

Allow longer read-only balance checks, query providers concurrently and place unsupported balances last. Expected unsupported Google balance checks stay neutral; zero or negative Phala credited funds show an alert.

actions.when: If serving Fal or WaveSpeedAI, or using the added video automatic-offer profiles, update the CLI then install the compatible signed worker. Existing manual offers keep their settings.
To use WaveSpeedAI, save its API key, check its balance and explicitly enable the models you want. Review and enable automatic-offer limits separately.
